ideas.question: Is there a developmental period during the first year of life where infants with maternal obesity have an increased risk for SUID compared to those without maternal obesity?
ideas.comparison: Cases from ncfrp_v51 (SUID cases) are compared within subgroups based on postconceptional age and whether the mother had obesity during pregnancy.
ideas.why_open: This study aims to explore a potential critical period where maternal obesity could disproportionately affect SUID risk. Such knowledge would allow targeted interventions aimed at high-risk periods in vulnerable infants.
ideas.data: Postconceptional age and maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) will be compared within SUID cases.

ideas.question: Does hospital overnight stay impact the risk of sudden unexpected infant death in infants with different gestational ages?
ideas.comparison: Cases from ncfrp_v51 are grouped based on whether the infant spent time in the hospital and their gestational age at birth.
ideas.why_open: This question examines if neonatal care practices, such as overnight stays post-delivery, influence SUID risk differently across gestational age groups. Understanding this could improve discharge policies and early home monitoring protocols.
ideas.data: Gestational age at birth (GESTREC3) and hospital overnight stay status will be compared within SUID cases.

ideas.question: Does prior pregnancy history modify the risk of sudden unexpected infant death among infants born to mothers with pre-existing medical conditions?
ideas.comparison: Cases from ncfrp_v51 are stratified based on whether the mother had a previous live birth and her health condition status.
ideas.why_open: Identifying if past pregnancies and maternal health impact SUID incidence can inform prenatal care strategies. This would help tailor interventions for women with complex obstetric histories.
ideas.data: Previous live birth history (GEST_WK_PU) and pre-existing medical conditions will be analyzed within SUID cases.

ideas.question: Does the presence of multiple gestation influence the risk pattern of sudden unexpected infant death throughout postconceptional age?
ideas.comparison: Cases from ncfrp_v51 are grouped based on whether they were part of a multiple gestation and their developmental trajectory.
ideas.why_open: This question aims to identify if being part of a twin or triplet set alters the risk of SUID over time. Such findings would be crucial for counseling families expecting multiples.
ideas.data: Multiple gestation status and postconceptional age will be analyzed within SUID cases.

ideas.question: Is there a significant difference in sudden unexpected infant death risk between infants who were breastfed exclusively versus those with mixed feeding methods?
ideas.comparison: Cases from ncfrp_v51 are stratified by whether the infant was exclusively breastfed or had mixed feeding practices.
ideas.why_open: Exploring if breastfeeding mode influences SUID could provide insights into early life nutrition's role in risk reduction. This would highlight important early intervention points for infant health.
ideas.data: Feeding method and postconceptional age will be analyzed within SUID cases.
